about: A non-normative profile: behaviour that a careful CESR parser shows but that no clause of the specification states, such as refusing a code its tables do not assign even when the code carries its own size. Every assertion is level INTEROP with a basis naming the inference it rests on, and passing it is never a conformance claim. This file is generated by scripts/regenerate from scenarios/cesr/ and must not be edited. Fields: name; normative (false); basis (what the profile's expectations rest on); cases (the case ids, in order).
basis: Inference from the CESR specification v1.0 (tag v1.0, commit 037129608b9e6960858b752019ac273d40d7386c): a parser cannot know what an unassigned code means, so it should refuse it rather than skip it by its size. No clause states this.
name: cesr-strict
